what_this_is: Proven post formats for artlab ONLY. Each account has its own cohort, its own formats and its own weekly review — nothing is shared between accounts, because the niches do not transfer. The agent fetches this file every run and assigns one format_slug per post; that slug flows into review-state, into the post's Notion row, and into the weekly scorer, which rolls outcomes up BY FORMAT. The format-level roll-up is the only level anyone should act on.
hard_rules: Borrow STRUCTURE, never AESTHETIC. Shot order, cut points, clip length, first frame, caption placement and sequencing are all fair to copy. Colour, grade, typography, styling, music and phrasing are not -- copying those produces another account in a category that already has plenty.

No shoots and no original photography. Every format below must be satisfiable from assets that already exist in the brand's asset bank. A format that needs new footage is not usable and must not be selected.
No AI-generated imagery. Using a model to find a pattern is research; using one to make the picture is not allowed.

cohort.source: ART Lab -- IG Engagement Targets (Notion, 28 accounts)
cohort.lanes: 3 core peers (robotics x art), 11 light, 14 interiors & spatial
cohort.note: Core peers carry the most weight despite being the smallest accounts -- they are the only ones doing what ART Lab does.

asset_banks.note: The 'ART Lab — Media Library' Notion database was ruled out by Isabel on 2026-08-26 because its assets are lamp renders that are not being used. The real source of ART Lab post assets is not yet known.

formats.name: The uninterrupted loop
formats.structure: One continuous motion. No cuts, no title card, no logo. 4-10 seconds, looping seamlessly.
formats.why_it_works: The viewer cannot immediately tell whether they are watching something alive or something driven, so they re-watch to decide. Highest completion rate available without a gimmick.
formats.evidence: Studio DRIFT's Shylight opens and closes on the nyctinastic rhythm of a real flower and has been on permanent display at the Rijksmuseum for years.
formats.notes: Satisfied by any single-motion clip in the Media Library. Do not cut it; do not add an intro card.

formats.name: Human and machine, same frame, same task
formats.structure: A person and a machine doing the SAME activity at the same time, both fully in shot. Not a person operating a device -- two agents doing one thing.
formats.first_frame: Both already engaged in the activity.
formats.why_it_works: Reads as a relationship rather than a product demo. This is the entire difference between how a robotics company is received and how an art practice is received.
formats.evidence: Sougwen Chung paints alongside her D.O.U.G. arms; coverage describes it as 'part team effort, part improvised dance'. Madeline Gannon's Mimus has no pre-planned path and follows visitors it finds interesting.
formats.notes: The strongest format in the set for ART Lab. Satisfied by the noticing/reacting assets, where the object and a person are both present and both acting.

formats.name: The mechanism reveal
formats.structure: Finished result first, then cut to the thing that produced it. Same subject, two angles. Result-then-mechanism, never the reverse.
formats.why_it_works: Converts spectacle into comprehension, and comprehension is what gets saved and sent rather than merely liked. Reversing the order turns a magic trick into an engineering post.
formats.evidence: Mimus documentation pairs the creature-like behaviour with the ceiling depth-sensor array that produces it. The watchmaking caseback shot is the same move.
formats.notes: Pair a finished-state asset with a close-up asset of the same subject. Both already exist in the bank -- this format is pure recombination.

formats.name: Scale betrayal
formats.structure: Open with no size reference -- no floor, no furniture, no hand. Hold. Then a human or a known object enters and the true scale lands in one beat.
formats.first_frame: The subject, filling the frame, size ambiguous.
formats.why_it_works: One cut, no caption needed, reliably re-watched. The cheapest format here to assemble and the most legible to an audience outside the art world.
formats.evidence: Landscape-scale fibre-optic fields and architectural light installations depend on this reveal for almost all their circulation.
formats.notes: Pair a close-up asset with a room-context asset of the same subject.

formats.name: State change as the whole post
formats.structure: At rest, then alive. 2-3 seconds, with the transition kept in -- never cut around it.
formats.first_frame: The resting state, held just long enough to register.
formats.why_it_works: Structurally identical to a fashion transition reel, so the grammar is already familiar to a general feed. That is why it travels beyond the art audience.
formats.evidence: Shylight's open/close cycle; Marcelis's lit-versus-unlit resin work.
formats.notes: Also satisfiable by pairing a day-state render with an evening-state render of the same subject.

formats.name: The catalogue plate
formats.structure: One subject, centred, generous negative space. Caption states the facts and stops. No question, no CTA.
formats.why_it_works: It will underperform on engagement every time, and it is still worth running occasionally, because a feed with no quiet frames reads as a brand rather than a practice.
formats.evidence: The smallest accounts in the light lane run this most -- which tells you exactly what it costs and what it buys.
formats.notes: Cap at one per fortnight. This format is a deliberate loss on engagement in exchange for register.
